Subject: Question on Invoice R-8892 — wire path & VAT

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the invoice (attached). We are preparing payment for Invoice R-8892 (EUR 62,400). Our treasury will likely send the wire from a US-based operating account and the bank intends to route through an intermediary which will convert from EUR to USD before reaching Redwood's account unless we instruct otherwise.

Before we proceed we need confirmation on three items:
1) Do you require Gross Received (i.e., sender to cover all correspondent/intermediary bank fees) or can we remit Net-of-fees and have Redwood invoice/credit the shortfall?
2) Does Redwood require the payment to land in an EUR account to avoid FX exposure on your side, or is it OK for you to accept USD?
3) VAT — we are EU-headquartered and will provide our VAT reg number if needed; should we expect any VAT on this invoice or will it be reverse-charged?

Attachment: Invoice-R-8892.pdf (PDF, 150KB)

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can instruct the bank today.

Best,
Marcel

Hi Marcel — thanks for the note and for sending the invoice. Looping in Laura (finance) and Marissa (payments) to confirm details, but high level:

- Preference: We prefer the invoice amount to be received gross (i.e., sender covers ALL bank and intermediary charges). That prevents reconciliation headaches and ensures the full EUR amount posts.
- Account preference: Our ideal is to receive EUR into our EUR account. If you must route via a USD intermediary that converts prior to our bank, Redwood would prefer you instruct the sending bank to mark charges as OUR (sender pays) rather than BEN or SHA.
- VAT: Laura will confirm the tax treatment; please include your VAT registration number in your reply.

I've attached our bank stub with the EUR account info and SWIFT rails (ben_bank_stub.pdf). If the sending bank cannot mark charges as OUR, let us know and we can quote the net/FX offset workflow.

Next steps: If you can confirm (a) VAT number, (b) whether bank will set OUR, we can confirm acceptance and expected clearance timeline.

Subject: VAT handling for Invoice R-8892

Hi Marcel — quick note from Finance on VAT:

- Redwood Inference (US HQ) does not charge EU VAT on B2B supplies when the buyer is a VAT-registered company in the EU and goods/services are provided cross-border.
- For Globex (B2B, EU), the treatment is "reverse charge"; you should self-account for VAT in your jurisdiction, so no VAT should be on the Redwood invoice.
- Please reply with your company VAT registration number and the billing legal entity name you will use for payment. We will then issue (or reissue) the invoice marked: \"VAT reverse-charge — VAT due by the recipient.\"

Note on documentation: we require a copy of your bank's payment confirmation or remittance advice once the wire is sent. If the payment is converted en route (EUR -> USD), please provide the intermediary bank's details and the exact debit amount so we can reconcile FX differences.

Attached: tax_form_request.docx — a one-page list of information we need to finalize tax notation on the invoice.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

Ben / Laura,

Thanks for the clarity. Our treasury confirmed the following: the outgoing instruction will be in EUR but our US bank's correspondent (Bank of Atlantic) will likely debit USD and convert at their posted rate (they do that for cross-border settlement). They offered two options:

A) We send EUR with OUR charges flagged — correspondent will pass full EUR to your account (no conversion).
B) We allow the correspondent to convert to USD (they will debit USD) and the payment will land in your USD nostro. In that case the correspondent subtracts a fee.

We prefer option B for operational simplicity. If Redwood can accept option B and absorb the correspondent fee / FX delta, we will proceed today. Otherwise we'll instruct Treasury to use option A and pay the sending bank fees to keep the EUR leg intact.

VAT number: GB123456789 (this is Globex EU trading entity). Billing name: Globex Industries Ltd.

Please confirm which option you prefer.

Best,
Marcel

Marcel — thanks for the quick follow. Final position from Redwood:

1) Primary request: please use option A (EUR delivered to our EUR account with charges marked OUR). That is the cleanest for reconciliation and avoids any FX charge on our side.
2) If Treasury cannot execute OUR and must use option B (correspondent converts to USD and fees are deducted), Redwood will accept the payment but we will treat any shortfall (difference between invoiced EUR amount and net received) as a deduction and issue a short credit/adjustment note only after reconciliation. We will also convert USD received back to EUR at our banking rate for internal accounting — there may be a small FX variance.
3) VAT: confirmed — we will reissue the invoice with "reverse charge" notation and no VAT. Laura has what she needs from your VAT number and billing entity.

Action items:
- Marcel: please confirm whether Treasury will instruct OUR (preferred) or will proceed with B. If B, send the intermediary bank's expected debit amount and fee stub once payment is made.
- Marissa/Finance: we'll await remittance and reconcile the net amount. If net < invoiced amount, we'll propose a small adjustment process (credit note) after clearance.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — happy to jump on a 15-min call if helpful.

Cheers,
